content: {"conclusions":[{"claim":"On the synthetic two-photo cases, the fixed template detector separates the canonical full and empty states and retains the full state under the tested noise, blur, and dimming transformations.","evidence":"detector-gap-2026-11-14.txt, first table, rows GENUINE full, GENUINE empty, GENUINE full noise .03, blur 1, and light x0.8: fill 0.95/0.03/0.90/0.92/0.84 respectively","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Whether the template detector is sufficient for a controlled demonstration and which real-shelf conditions must be tested next.","caveat":"These transformations of template imagery do not establish recognition of the team's actual shelf products or robustness to real camera variation."},{"claim":"A four-pixel shift breaks the fixed detector's full-state classification, while the shift-tolerant variant repairs both tested shift cases.","evidence":"detector-gap-2026-11-14.txt, first table, GENUINE full shifted 2 px and shifted 4 px: fill 0.70 and 0.61 with states full and low; shift-tolerant table: fill_shift 0.94 and 0.94 with r_shift 1.02 and 1.01","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Whether to retain shift-tolerant matching as the default candidate for subsequent testing.","caveat":"Only two synthetic translations up to four pixels are reported; rotation, scale, perspective, occlusion, and real mounting movement remain untested."},{"claim":"The shift-tolerant variant preserves a synthetic fill gradient for column removal, but its values are not calibrated to actual shelf quantity.","evidence":"detector-gap-2026-11-14.txt, shift-tolerant distances table, GENUINE 1/3, 1/2, and 2/3 removed: fill_shift 0.63, 0.51, and 0.40","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Whether fill can be used as a demo state signal rather than as a trustworthy inventory count or reorder quantity.","caveat":"Column removal and blending are artificial proxies; no mapping to real product counts, planogram changes, or consumption has been validated."},{"claim":"The detector does not safely reject all unrelated inputs: one unrelated full-slot photograph is classified full, and several unrelated or occluded scenes produce low states.","evidence":"detector-gap-2026-11-14.txt, first table, UNRELATED slot1 full photo: state full, fill 0.77; UNRELATED recorded scene, half covered, third covered, and hand: state low; shift-tolerant table, slot1 full photo: fill_shift 0.88","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Whether detector output may trigger autonomous replenishment or must remain advisory with human approval and additional guards.","caveat":"The unrelated set is small and not necessarily representative, but the observed false full and low outputs are sufficient to rule out an unsupported safety claim."},{"claim":"The board baseline shows modest resource use for the deployed application during one sampled workload, not detector throughput.","evidence":"board-baseline-2026-11-14.md, measurement table: app process CPU 13.5% of one core over a 5 s sample; container 13.2% CPU and 77.5 MiB; process RSS 131,664 KiB","evidence_class":"measured-infrastructure","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"Whether the current application can remain deployed on the UNO Q while accuracy and performance experiments proceed.","caveat":"Frames came from the laptop camera page, sampling was brief, and no per-frame latency, processed FPS, sustained-load, or power measurement was taken."},{"claim":"Real-time on-device detection and local feasibility of a learned model remain unmeasured.","evidence":"board-baseline-2026-11-14.md, final paragraph: per-frame classification time, actual processed FPS, and power not measured; no learned model has run on the board","evidence_class":"measured-infrastructure","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"What performance claims may appear in the pitch and whether a learned-model workstream should be attempted before the demo.","caveat":"The baseline neither proves nor disproves feasibility; it only identifies the missing measurements."},{"claim":"No result in the supplied output constitutes validated recognition of the team's real shelf products.","evidence":"detector-gap-2026-11-14.txt, both tables contain GENUINE template transformations and UNRELATED scenes; board-baseline-2026-11-14.md states that accuracy must be established on real recordings","evidence_class":"synthetic","supported":"yes","decision_informed":"How to label demo evidence and whether to claim shelf autonomy, production readiness, or only a synthetic prototype result.","caveat":"The label GENUINE must not be presented as real-shelf validation; the supplied context explicitly says validated recordings do not yet exist."}],"unsupported_or_overstated":["The detector recognizes or reliably tracks the team's real Valio shelf products.","The shift-tolerant detector is robust to camera movement or real shelf conditions; only synthetic translations up to four pixels were tested.","Unrelated objects, hands, and occlusions are safely rejected; the table includes an unrelated input classified full and several classified low.","Fill values represent actual inventory levels or can determine reorder quantities without calibration.","The UNO Q measurements demonstrate real-time detection, end-to-end camera performance, power suitability, or production readiness.","Low CPU and memory use establish that a learned detector can run locally; no learned model has run on the board.","These results validate unattended replenishment or scheduled ordering; false full and low states argue against unattended actuation, and the replenishment proposal remains unvalidated."],"repetitive_or_low_value":["In a team summary, drop the duplicate per-case r_shift values for unshifted cases where they merely repeat the first table; retain one compact before/after comparison and the failure cases.","Collapse the five similar synthetic GENUINE full-variant rows into one range, while preserving the shifted and unrelated failures as separate rows.","Drop container network totals of 53.6 MB in and 1.95 MB out from the decision summary; they are cumulative since startup and do not inform accuracy, latency, or feasibility.","Avoid repeating both CPU figures without explanation; retain the 5 s process sample and container statistic only in the detailed appendix."],"negative_results":["The fixed detector changes GENUINE full shifted 4 px from full to low, showing sensitivity to small synthetic misalignment.","UNRELATED slot1 full photo is classified full by the fixed rule and remains near-full at fill_shift 0.88 with shift-tolerant matching.","Unrelated recorded scene, half-covered scene, third-covered scene, and a smooth hand blob are classified low, which could cause false replenishment if low directly triggers an order.","Unrelated noise and other-object inputs become uncertain rather than receiving a reliable reject state.","No per-frame classification time, actual processed FPS, or power measurement exists.","No learned model has run on the UNO Q.","No validated real recordings of the team's shelf products underpin the detector results."],"open_question_worth_a_run":["Record a labeled UNO Q camera dataset of the actual shelf products covering full, empty, several real removal levels, camera shifts, lighting changes, hands/occlusion, unrelated objects, and planogram changes. Run fixed and shift-tolerant detectors unchanged and report the full state-confusion matrix, false-full and false-low rates on non-target inputs, and uncertain rate; do not tune thresholds on the final test split.","On the UNO Q with the intended camera and target observation cadence, run a sustained detection workload and measure per-frame p50/p95 latency, actually processed FPS, CPU, memory, temperature/throttling if available, and power, including behavior when frames arrive faster than they can be processed."]}
